newsitem.title: SWEDEN: GOLF-HAEGGMAN SINKS LAST-HOLE CHIP FOR COURSE RECORD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-HAEGGMAN SINKS LAST-HOLE CHIP FOR COURSE RECORD.

text.p: Joakim Haeggman chipped in at the last hole on the Barseback course on Saturday to take a four-shot lead with a course record-tieing 65 in the Scandinavian Masters.

The 27-year-old Swede's spectacular finish to the third round delighted a partisan 30,000 gallery and pulled him four clear of 1993 European Ryder Cup teammate Peter Baker of England and Australian Stephen Allan.

Haeggman's seven-under-par round after sharing the overnight lead with seven other players took him to 15-under-par 201, with Baker, one of the seven, carding 69 and 23-year-old tour rookie Allan a 66.
Veteran Spaniard Jose Rivero is a further stroke back on 206 and his young compatriot Ignacio Garrido kept up his Ryder Cup bid by holding a share of fifth place on 207 after a 71.

Garrido birdied two of the last three holes to stay alive in his bid to follow in his father Antonio's Ryder Cup footsteps by clinching his place in the team for Valderrama next month against the Americans.

Compatriot Jose Maria Olazabal, however, had one more indifferent day with his irons and his vital 10th and last automatic place on Europe's table is now under great threat. His 71 left him 13 shots off the pace
Garrido is 16th in the table and he and Ireland's Padraig Harrington in 11th spot could go past Olazabal, whom Ballesteros hopes will qualify to leave him a free hand with his two wild cards.
British Open joint runner-up Jesper Parnevik, who cannot qualify for European points because he is U.S.-based and needs to be picked, was disappointed to shoot only 71. He is eight behind Haeggman.
For Haeggman, it was a return to form after being in a trough since his heady days of 1993.

It looked as if he might be caught by Baker, who had closed to within a stroke of him as the Swede went to the 17th. But the Englishman dropped a stroke on 17 and Haeggman's grandstand birdie-birdie finish, including the chip-in, bolstered his lead.

"I drove into trees and had to hit around them to get to the green, bending my six-iron badly in the process," said Haeggman. "When the ball went to the fringe at the back of the green I feared the worst, but it came out perfectly and looked in all the way.

"I'm now checking how I can mend my six-iron legally for the last round because I want everything right. I've been waiting for a big event like this for three years to shine and the huge crowds here have given me just the right motivation."
The other British Open runner-up, Northern Irishman Darren Clarke, can now pass Ian Woosnam on top of the European rankings if he secures fifth place from being only four strokes out of second spot.
Colin Montgomerie, 212, and lying fourth on the European rankings, shot 69 and can also make up ground on Woosnam, who missed the cut, in pursuit of a record fifth Order of Merit title.
